bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Lean 60 percent of body weight onto the front foot, bring the stock up to the cheek before the shoulder, and swing from the hips.
core_mechanism_bullets: Lean 60 percent of body weight onto the front foot, bring the stock up to the cheek before the shoulder, and swing from the hips.
Use Swing-Through, Sustained Lead, or Pull-Away lead methods and continue moving the barrel through the target path after pulling the trigger.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: A standard 108-millimeter clay pigeon launched at 42 miles per hour travels 61.6 feet per second, requiring 2 to 3 feet of forward lead on crossing shots.

primary_source_citation.title: NRA Misfire Wait and Bore Obstruction Clearing Standard Technical Reference

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Hold the shotgun pointed downrange for 30 seconds after any click or misfire and listen for quiet pop squib loads that leave a wad in the bore.
core_mechanism_bullets: Hold the shotgun pointed downrange for 30 seconds after any click or misfire and listen for quiet pop squib loads that leave a wad in the bore.
Unload immediately and look through the barrel from the breech end if mud, snow, or a stuck plastic wad is suspected of blocking the bore.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: Hitting at least 12 out of 25 clay targets on two rounds of trap from the 16-yard stations demonstrates consistent cheek weld and follow-through.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Demonstrate the 30-second hangfire hold, open the action of a dummy training shotgun, and inspect the bore for obstructions.
bespoke_clusters.real_world_connection_box: NRA Misfire Wait and Bore Obstruction Clearing Standard: Hold the shotgun pointed downrange for 30 seconds after any click or misfire and listen for quiet pop squib loads that leave a wad in the bore.
